nodes.summary: A continuous scalar kernel has a continuous feature map `x ↦ k(·, x)` into `H`, as `‖φ(x) - φ(y)‖² = k(x, x) - 2 k(x, y) + k(y, y)` (via Mathlib's `RKHS.continuous_kernel_iff_continuous_kerFun`; continuity of `k` is part of universality in Theorem 5 of Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012)).
nodes.title: Continuity of the feature map

nodes.summary: For a sample `x₁, …, x_m`, the empirical mean embedding is `μ_X = (1/m) ∑ᵢ φ(xᵢ)` (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), Section 2.2, before equation (5)).
nodes.title: Empirical mean embedding

nodes.summary: The function `φ(y)` takes the value `k(x, y)` at `x`: `φ(y)(x) = k(x, y)` (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), Section 2.2).
nodes.title: Kernel functions are feature maps

nodes.summary: The feature map sends `x` to the kernel function `φ(x) = k(·, x) ∈ H`, the representer of evaluation at `x` (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), Section 2.2).
nodes.title: Canonical feature map of a reproducing kernel Hilbert space

nodes.summary: `⟪μ_X, μ_Y⟫ = (1/(mn)) ∑ᵢ ∑ⱼ k(xᵢ, yⱼ)` (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), derivation of equation (5)).
nodes.title: Inner product of empirical mean embeddings

nodes.summary: `⟪f, μ_X⟫ = (1/m) ∑ᵢ f(xᵢ)` (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), Section 2.2, before equation (5)).
nodes.title: Reproducing property of the empirical mean embedding

nodes.summary: For every `f ∈ H`, `⟪f, φ(x)⟫ = f(x)` (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), Section 2.2).
nodes.title: Reproducing property of the feature map

nodes.summary: If the feature map is Bochner integrable for the s-finite measures `P` and `Q`, then `⟪μ_P, μ_Q⟫ = E_{(x, y) ~ P ⊗ Q} k(x, y)` (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), proof of Lemma 6).
nodes.title: Inner product of mean embeddings as an expectation over independent copies

nodes.summary: If the feature map is Bochner integrable for `P` and `Q`, then `⟪μ_P, μ_Q⟫ = ∫∫ k(x, y) dP(x) dQ(y)` (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), proof of Lemma 6).
nodes.title: Inner product of two mean embeddings

nodes.summary: Reproducing property of the kernel mean embedding (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), Lemma 3). If the feature map is Bochner integrable for `μ`, then `⟪f, μ_P⟫ = ∫ f dP` for every `f ∈ H`.
nodes.title: Reproducing property of the kernel mean embedding

nodes.summary: If `φ` is Bochner integrable for `μ`, then every `f ∈ H` is `μ`-integrable, since `f(x) = ⟪f, φ(x)⟫` (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), proof of Lemma 3).
nodes.title: Elements of an RKHS are integrable against measures with integrable feature map

nodes.summary: On a compact metric space with its Borel σ-algebra, a continuous feature map is Bochner integrable for every finite measure, so the mean embedding of every Borel probability measure exists (the setting of Theorem 5 of Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012)).
nodes.title: Mean embeddings exist for continuous kernels on compact spaces

nodes.summary: Existence of the kernel mean embedding (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), Lemma 3). If the feature map is strongly measurable and `∫ √k(x, x) dP(x) < ∞`, then the feature map is Bochner integrable, so the mean embedding `μ_P ∈ H` exists and has the reproducing property. The paper assumes `k` measurable; the measurability hypothesis here is the one Bochner integration needs.
nodes.title: Existence of the kernel mean embedding

nodes.summary: If the feature map is Bochner integrable for the s-finite measures `P` and `Q`, then `(x, y) ↦ k(x, y)` is `P ⊗ Q`-integrable, since `|k(x, y)| ≤ ‖φ(x)‖ ‖φ(y)‖` (used in the proof of Lemma 6 of Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012)).
nodes.title: Integrability of the kernel on a product

nodes.summary: The unbiased MMD statistic is unbiased (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), Lemma 6). Let `P` and `Q` be probability measures with Bochner integrable feature maps, and let `x₁, …, x_m` be i.i.d. from `P` and `y₁, …, y_n` i.i.d. from `Q`, independent, with `m, n ≥ 2`. Then `E[MMD_u²] = MMD(P, Q)²`.
nodes.title: The unbiased MMD statistic is unbiased

nodes.summary: Characterization of characteristic translation-invariant kernels (Sriperumbudur, Gretton, Fukumizu, Schölkopf and Lanckriet, *Hilbert space embeddings and metrics on probability measures*, JMLR 11 (2010), Theorem 9). Let `d ≥ 1` and let `H` be a real RKHS on `ℝ^d` whose kernel is `k(x, y) = ψ(x - y)` with `ψ(x) = ∫ exp(-i xᵀω) dΛ(ω)` for a finite Borel measure `Λ`, so that `ψ` is a bounded continuous real…
nodes.title: Characterization of characteristic translation-invariant kernels

nodes.summary: Universal kernels are characteristic (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), Theorem 5 and the discussion after it). On a compact metric space, a continuous kernel whose RKHS is dense in `C(X)` is characteristic.
nodes.title: Universal kernels are characteristic

nodes.summary: Characteristic kernel (Fukumizu et al. 2008; Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), Section 2.2, after Theorem 5). The kernel of `H` is characteristic if the mean embedding is injective on probability measures with integrable feature map.
nodes.title: Characteristic kernel

nodes.summary: On the closed unit ball of a real inner product space, `f ↦ ⟪f, v⟫` attains its supremum `‖v‖` (the Cauchy–Schwarz step in the proof of Lemma 4 of Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012)).
nodes.title: The unit ball attains the norm of a vector

nodes.summary: Every kernel matrix `(k(xᵢ, xⱼ))ᵢⱼ` of `k(x, y) = ⟪φ(x), φ(y)⟫` is positive semidefinite, the converse direction of Aronszajn's theorem (F. Bach, *Learning Theory from First Principles*, MIT Press (2024), Section 7.3, Proposition 7.3).
nodes.title: The kernel of an RKHS is a positive-definite kernel

nodes.summary: For a real scalar RKHS, Mathlib's operator-valued kernel `RKHS.kernel H x y` is multiplication by the scalar kernel `k(x, y) = ⟪φ(x), φ(y)⟫` (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), Section 2.2).
nodes.title: Operator-valued and scalar kernels

nodes.summary: The Gram matrix `RepresenterTheorem.kernelGram` used for kernel ridge regression has entries `k(xᵢ, xⱼ) = kernelValue H xᵢ xⱼ` (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), Section 2.2: `⟪φ(x), φ(y)⟫ = k(x, y)`).
nodes.title: The kernel Gram matrix of the representer theorem

nodes.summary: `k(x, y) = k(y, x)` (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), Section 2.2).
nodes.title: Symmetry of the kernel

nodes.summary: The kernel is the inner product of feature maps, `k(x, y) = ⟪φ(x), φ(y)⟫` (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), Section 2.2).
nodes.title: Scalar kernel of a real reproducing kernel Hilbert space

nodes.summary: The mean embedding as a function (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), Lemma 3 and its proof). If the feature map is Bochner integrable for `μ`, the mean embedding is the function `μ_P(t) = ∫ k(t, x) dP(x)`.
nodes.title: The mean embedding as a function

nodes.summary: The mean embedding of a measure `P` is the Bochner integral `μ_P = ∫ φ(x) dP(x)` of the feature map; it is the element of `H` representing expectation under `P` (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), Section 2.2 and Lemma 3). The definition is meaningful when the feature map is integrable, see `inner_meanEmbedding`.
nodes.title: Kernel mean embedding

nodes.summary: For `i ≠ j`, the pair `(xᵢ, xⱼ)` of an i.i.d. sample from `P` has law `P ⊗ P` (the independent copies `x, x'` of Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), Lemma 6).
nodes.title: Two coordinates of an i.i.d. sample are independent copies

nodes.summary: (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), Section 2.2, before equation (5)): `MMD_b = ‖μ_X - μ_Y‖`.
nodes.title: The biased empirical MMD is the distance between empirical mean embeddings

nodes.summary: The biased empirical MMD as a V-statistic (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), equation (5)): `MMD_b² = (1/m²) ∑_{i,j} k(xᵢ, xⱼ) - (2/(mn)) ∑_{i,j} k(xᵢ, yⱼ) + (1/n²) ∑_{i,j} k(yᵢ, yⱼ)`.
nodes.title: The biased empirical MMD as a V-statistic

nodes.summary: Biased empirical MMD (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), equation (2), with `F` the unit ball of `H`). For samples `x₁, …, x_m` and `y₁, …, y_n`, `MMD_b = sup_{‖f‖ ≤ 1} ((1/m) ∑ᵢ f(xᵢ) - (1/n) ∑ⱼ f(yⱼ))`.
nodes.title: Biased empirical MMD

nodes.summary: Symmetry of the MMD (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), Section 2.2; pseudometric axioms as in its footnote 3). If the feature map is Bochner integrable for `P` and `Q`, then `MMD(P, Q) = MMD(Q, P)`.
nodes.title: Symmetry of the MMD

nodes.summary: The MMD is the distance between mean embeddings (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), Lemma 4). If the feature map is Bochner integrable for `P` and `Q`, then `MMD(P, Q) = ‖μ_P - μ_Q‖`.
nodes.title: The MMD is the distance between mean embeddings

nodes.summary: The MMD of a characteristic kernel separates probability measures (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), Section 2.2). For a characteristic kernel and probability measures with integrable feature map, `MMD(P, Q) = 0` if and only if `P = Q`. For every kernel the MMD is a pseudometric on such measures; it is a metric exactly when the kernel is characteristic.
nodes.title: The MMD of a characteristic kernel separates probability measures

nodes.summary: The MMD of a universal kernel characterizes distributions (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), Theorem 5). Let `X` be a compact metric space with its Borel σ-algebra and `H` a universal RKHS on `X`: its kernel `k` is continuous and `H` is dense in `C(X)` for the supremum norm. Then for Borel probability measures `P` and `Q`, `MMD(P, Q) = 0` if and only if `P = Q`.
nodes.title: The MMD of a universal kernel characterizes distributions

nodes.summary: Triangle inequality for the MMD (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), Section 2.2; pseudometric axioms as in its footnote 3). If the feature map is Bochner integrable for `P`, `Q` and `R`, then `MMD(P, R) ≤ MMD(P, Q) + MMD(Q, R)`.
nodes.title: Triangle inequality for the MMD

nodes.summary: The MMD vanishes on the diagonal (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), Section 2.2; pseudometric axioms as in its footnote 3). If the feature map is Bochner integrable for `P`, then `MMD(P, P) = 0`.
nodes.title: The MMD vanishes on the diagonal

nodes.summary: Population MMD in terms of the kernel (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), Lemma 6). If the feature map is Bochner integrable for the s-finite measures `P` and `Q`, then, with `x, x'` independent with law `P` and `y, y'` independent with law `Q`, `MMD(P, Q)² = E k(x, x') - 2 E k(x, y) + E k(y, y')`.
nodes.title: Population MMD in terms of the kernel

nodes.summary: Unbiased empirical estimate of the squared MMD (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), Lemma 6, equation (3)). For samples `x₁, …, x_m` and `y₁, …, y_n`, `MMD_u² = 1/(m(m-1)) ∑_{i ≠ j} k(xᵢ, xⱼ) + 1/(n(n-1)) ∑_{i ≠ j} k(yᵢ, yⱼ)
nodes.title: Unbiased empirical estimate of the squared MMD

nodes.summary: Maximum mean discrepancy over the unit ball of an RKHS (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), Definition 2, equation (1), with `F` the unit ball of `H`). `MMD(P, Q) = sup_{‖f‖ ≤ 1} (∫ f dP - ∫ f dQ)`.
nodes.title: Maximum mean discrepancy over the unit ball of an RKHS

nodes.summary: `‖φ(x)‖ = √k(x, x)` (Gretton et al., *A kernel two-sample test*, JMLR 13 (2012), proof of Lemma 3).
nodes.title: Norm of a feature map
